title: VerilogCoder: Autonomous Verilog Coding Agents with Graph-based Planning and Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)-based Waveform Tracing Tool

model.params_source: paper 'Main Results' ('The temperature and top_p parameters of the LLMs are set to 0.1 and 1.0, respectively'); max_tokens assumed (Verilog modules plus Thought-Action-Observation turns)

task.subset_rule: all 156 VerilogEval-Human v2 specification-to-RTL problems; VerilogCoder is run once per problem
task.approximation: cannot be expressed by the runner: one claim item is a whole multi-agent session, not a single call (see open_points)

items.source: VerilogEval-Human v2 (Pinckney et al. 2024), 156 specification-to-RTL problems with golden testbenches; the agent framework is at https://github.com/NVlabs/VerilogCoder

fields.label: golden testbench - pass/fail comes from simulation, not string comparison

prompt.source_location: Section 'Experimental Results' ('We use the same planning, coding, and debugging prompts for these 156 problems'); Figure 4 shows one example Thought-Action-Observation interaction

output.parse: free text -> the final Verilog module extracted by the framework

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: Verilog functional correctness pass-rate = #passed / #total over the 156 problems, one VerilogCoder run per problem
metric.judge: rule (Verilog simulation against the golden testbench)
metric.original_location: Table 1, row 'VerilogCoder (GPT-4 Turbo)' (VerilogCoder (Llama3) 67.3; plain GPT-4 Turbo 60.3)

cost.est_note: hand estimate: about 10 calls per problem x 156 problems on gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 with long agent transcripts. Highly uncertain - the loop length is data-dependent. No prepare run: the claim is not expressible as a run config.

open_points: Agentic, multi-call method. The claim is the pass-rate of a whole multi-agent system (task-graph planner, coder, AST-based waveform tracing tool, iterative debugging loop) built on Autogen; each of the 156 problems consumes an unbounded number of interdependent calls whose contents depend on simulator feedback. The Tier B runner executes exactly one independent call per item, so this claim cannot be expressed as a run config - it needs the released framework driven directly.

Scoring needs a local toolchain. Functional correctness is decided by compiling and simulating the generated Verilog against the golden testbench (e.g. iverilog), which is outside the runner and a human decision about local tooling.
Prompts not printed. The planning / coding / debugging role prompts have to be read out of the released repository, and the AST waveform tracing tool's observations are part of the prompt stream.
notes: The non-agentic row in the same table, 'GPT-4 Trubo [sic] 60.3', is a pass@1 number quoted from Pinckney et al. (2024) rather than measured here, so it is not an alternative claim for this paper either.
